newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 4.

text.p: General Motors Corp and the Canadian Automobile Workers union were divided over outsourcing the making of parts as more than 10,000 workers went on strike, shutting down car and trucks assembly lines, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
* Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co plans to buy KinderCare Learning Centers Inc for about $470 million or $20.25 a share, plus debt assumption.
* Ford Motor Co reported a 7.3 percent increase in September sales of its cars and light trucks.

* Digital Equipment Corp's chairman and chief executive officer told workers he did not plan to fill the leading position in the company's computer operations division, which has been left vacant since July.
* Bethlehem Steel Corp hired Salomon Brothers to determine whether it should sell, close or keep running three units.
* The cable television industry agreed to standardize new digital set top boxes.
* Authentic Fitness Corp reported steep losses for its quarter and year, saying it would close its skiwear business and eight outlet stores.
* Peat Marwick's new chief executive officer plans to make changes at the accounting and consulting firm.
* The U.S. government agreed to rescue a pension fund in the suit industry.
* U.S. mergers and acquisitions totalled $153.7 billion in the quarter, the third highest level ever.
* U.S. factory orders fell by 1.9 percent in August, the largest drop in more than three years.
* Goldman Sachs & Co is to find potential buyers for more than $3 billion of equipment lease backed securities being sold by AT&T Corp's AT&T Capital Corp early next week.
* Market skeptics wonder if any stock is reliably steady as shares in Nabisco Holdings of RJR Nabisco Holdings are selling for about 24 times this year's expected earnings.
* The Dow Jones industrials recouped early losses to end 1.12 points lower at 5932.85, while bonds ended little changed as investors awaited September employment figures.
* Monsanto Co's stock hit a record high amid early signs that crops planted with a genetically altered seed were performing better than expected.
